sections.h2: Which offices run property tax in Adair County, KY?
sections.html:
Adair County divides the job between two offices. One of them, the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), assigns each parcel its worth, while the sheriff is the one who receives payment. The rate itself is voted by the bodies that levy the tax, such as the fiscal court and the school board.

Find the PVA on Public Square in Columbia: 424 Public Square, Suite 2, KY 42728, telephone (270) 384-3673, weekdays eight to four. Deputies there process deed transfers, including partial sales, and adjust vehicle values. On the same contact page the county lists the sheriff at (270) 384-2776 and the County Clerk at (270) 384-2801.

Kentucky freezes the picture on January 1: a parcel is appraised as it was that morning. Anyone closing in February will usually find the year's bill addressed to the seller, so the Adair County sale contract ought to spell out who repays whom.

sections.h2: When must Adair County tax bills be paid?
sections.html:
The sheriff takes payment through every stage of the statutory calendar in KRS 134.015. The table shows what each stage costs.

Adair County bill payment stages, statewide schedule (source: KRS 134.015)
Payment windowWhat you owe
On or before November 1Face amount less 2 percent
November 2 to December 31Face amount
January 1 to January 31Face amount plus 5 percent
After January 31Face amount plus 10 percent

If the state delays bill mailing, it may substitute a shifted calendar built on one-month blocks. Whatever remains unpaid at the end of the collection season, April 15 under the normal schedule, goes to the County Clerk with a recorded lien.

sections.h2: What would an Adair County owner actually pay?
sections.html:
Frankfort levies 10.6 cents for every $100 of assessed value in 2025, a cut from 10.9 cents in 2024. Put that against a $150,800 house, the Census midpoint for Adair County, and the state portion is roughly $159.85. Other taxing bodies add their own rates, so ask the PVA or the sheriff for the combined total on a given address.

The homestead exemption changes the math for older owners. If the assessment drops to $101,700 after the exemption, the state share falls to about $107.80. Paying early trims 2 percent off whatever the total turns out to be.

Those numbers matter in a sale because the year's bill has to be divided between buyer and seller somewhere. Ask the closing agent how the contract handles it, and ask the sheriff what has already been paid on the account.

sections.h2: How does an Adair County owner challenge a value?
sections.html:
An owner who wants to appeal must first confer with the PVA or a deputy. Public viewing of the roll starts on the first Monday in May and lasts through the following two weeks. Raise a disputed value then, or earlier if notices have already gone out.

  • The PVA is required to explain how your number was derived, and the meeting is documented in writing.
  • The appeal itself is filed at the County Clerk's office, with a deadline one workday after viewing wraps up.
  • Gather proof: descriptions of the land and buildings, insurance papers, building costs and comparable listings or sales. Without it the board turns the appeal down.
  • Attend the hearing, which comes a few weeks later. Filing and then not appearing forfeits later review by the Kentucky Claims Commission.

A paid representative has to fall into a listed category, for example an attorney, CPA, licensed broker or certified appraiser, and must bring your written authorization. If the board lands above the figure you claimed, you receive a supplemental bill for the gap.

sections.h2: Can an older Adair County owner reduce the tax base?
sections.html:
Yes, through the homestead exemption. People 65 and older, along with owners the law classes as totally disabled, receive a deduction that the state Revenue Department fixed at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. Apply that to $150,800, the Census median home value here, and the taxed amount falls to $101,700.

File the form with the Adair County PVA during the year you want relief, by post, fax or email. The PVA accepts a driver's license, Medicare card or birth certificate as proof of age, with a Kentucky license or state ID covering residence. A household gets one exemption, and one spouse reaching 65 satisfies the age test.

Once approved, the exemption continues while the applicant stays in the home as owner. After a sale, the seller should notify the PVA so it is removed from the old address and can be requested for a new one.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell an Adair County house with taxes unpaid?
sections.html:
Selling does not erase an overdue balance. KRS 134.015 makes the tax the owner's own debt starting on the assessment date, and the parcel stays liened until payment or the expiry of the eleven-year span in KRS 134.420. A new deed does not change that. A title search will surface the lien, which is why the sheriff's payoff figure is worth getting before listing day.

While the County Clerk holds the account, each month adds 1 percent interest. The clerk and the county attorney take commissions, and a recording fee for the lien is added. Two notices go out by mail. Certificates can go on sale from 90 to 135 days after the handoff, and whoever buys one at that sale may add fees.

Paying the sheriff before April 15 avoids those clerk-stage extras completely.

sections.h2: What is Adair County, Kentucky, like for a seller?
sections.html:
Green County gave up part of its land in 1801 to create Adair County, whose lone municipality, Columbia, serves as seat. Roughly 405 square miles of land lie on the Pennyroyal Plateau, over 40 percent of it wooded. The Green River drains the county, and its impoundment as Green River Lake anchors a state park shared with Taylor County.

Farming drives the local economy: livestock, dairy, corn and tobacco. Road access improved a great deal once the Cumberland Parkway opened in 1973. Students attend Adair County Schools from the primary center to the high school. Census QuickFacts supplies these numbers:

  • 2025 population: 19,423, a gain of 2.8 percent over 2020.
  • Owner-occupied share of housing: 77.2 percent.
  • Home value at the midpoint: $150,800.
  • Household income at the midpoint is $53,553, and the poverty rate is 21.2 percent.
  • Gross rent at the midpoint: $771.

Neighbors on the map are Green, Taylor, Casey, Russell, Cumberland and Metcalfe counties. Columbia keeps Central time while Taylor and Casey counties to the north run on Eastern, a detail worth remembering when scheduling a closing with out-of-county parties. Rural areas hold 73.5 percent of the population, and the Census counted 7,136 households of 2.51 people on average.

The county recorded just six building permits in 2025, so nearly every sale involves a house that already stands. Where a house needs repairs or owes back taxes, selling for cash as-is lets both be cleared at a single closing.

faqs.q: When is the discount deadline for Adair County property taxes?
faqs.a: November 1 is the cutoff. Paying the whole bill by then saves 2 percent, the face amount applies from November 2 into December, and penalties start with the new year.

faqs.q: Who takes payment of Adair County tax bills?
faqs.a: Pay the Adair County Sheriff, whom the county lists at (270) 384-2776. The PVA, reachable at (270) 384-3673, only values property and never takes payments.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead exemption in Adair County?
faqs.a: The Department of Revenue fixed it at $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 years, deducted from the assessed figure. Owners 65 or older, or totally disabled, apply at the PVA in Columbia.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Adair County assessment after the deadline?
faqs.a: Not once the viewing period is over. The conference with the PVA must happen first, and the clerk filing is due the next workday after viewing ends. Viewing begins the first Monday of May and runs 13 days.

faqs.q: What happens if Adair County taxes go unpaid?
faqs.a: Once April 15 passes, the county clerk holds it as a certificate of delinquency backed by a recorded lien. Interest of 1 percent monthly accrues, and the certificate may be sold between 90 and 135 days after the handoff.
